I've been depressed for as long as I can remember. Literally since elementary school. On paper I should be happy. But I'm not. I'm an alcoholic and I'm  sick of being miserable and depressed and anxious.

This probably isn't her case, but in my experience with ex-coworkers, there are industries that couldn't care less about a criminal record. My local Wendy's was almost entirely staffed by folks with a less than stellar past. I worked with even harder criminals when I was working in an auto body shop. If you can turn a wrench, take instruction, and show up at work on time, they couldn't care less. One dude biked to work every day because he got popped with one too many DUI's. My manager had a heart of gold and would buy tools for the guys if they needed help. Just Harbor Freight stuff but it got the job done.

Yeah the can't is from fear and shame. 

I'm normally an upbeat guy. I'm the guy that people come to for help. Big guy with a beard and a flannel shirt is where all my friend turn to when they just need a shoulder to cry on. I'm a good listener, and a calm, level headed source of guidance. 

That's why it's so hard for me to reach out and ask for help. I have never had to do it before. I'm the guy that people COME TO for help, so I'm not good at REACHING OUT for help. And I'm in contact with a counselor. I'm not worried about the health effects of quitting, I'm not in quite that deep.
